title: Hybridisation: domains, geometry and model choice
subject: Chemistry
scope_summary: Grade 11 introductory hybridisation and bonding-model slice for Issue #31: central-atom electron-domain counting, sp2/sp3 set size, tetrahedral domain geometry, Lewis-to-3D translation, VSEPR versus orbital-overlap model scope, and sigma/pi overlap geometry. Advanced delocalisation and exception chemistry are outside this packet.

relations.expression: electron-domain count = bonded-neighbour regions + lone-pair regions on the chosen central atom
relations.meaning: VSEPR domain counting is local to the selected centre. A single, double or triple bond to one neighbour occupies one region/direction.

symbols.meaning: number of electron-density regions around the selected central atom

conditions: Choose the central atom before counting.
Treat each bonded neighbour as one region regardless of bond order.

derivation.why_valid: The count is local to one centre.

derivation.action: Count each bonded neighbour once and add lone pairs on that centre.
derivation.why_valid: VSEPR counts regions of electron density, not drawn bond lines.

derivation.action: Check that neighbour lone pairs were excluded.
derivation.why_valid: They belong to domains centred on those neighbours.

limits: Do not count lone pairs on terminal atoms when the question asks for domains around the central atom.
checks: A double bond to one neighbour must not create a second direction.

relations.expression: 3 electron-domain directions ↔ sp2 ↔ 3 hybrids; 4 directions ↔ sp3 ↔ 4 hybrids
relations.meaning: In the introductory valence-bond model, the number of hybrid orbitals equals the number of atomic orbitals combined and matches the modelled electron-domain directions.

symbols.meaning: one s plus two p orbitals combined
one s plus three p orbitals combined

conditions: Use this as an introductory local bonding model, not as a complete quantum description.

derivation.why_valid: Hybrid set choice follows the directional set being modelled.

derivation.action: Map three directions to sp2 and four to sp3.
derivation.why_valid: One s orbital is included in both labels, so set size is 3 or 4 respectively.

derivation.action: Check set size equals the number of modelled directions.
derivation.why_valid: The superscript alone is not the number of hybrids.

limits: The model rationalises directional bonding; it is not a full many-electron wavefunction description.
checks: sp2 must give three hybrids and sp3 four.

relations.expression: four electron domains → tetrahedral electron-domain arrangement; molecular geometry omits lone-pair positions from the atom-only name
relations.meaning: A flat Lewis structure records connectivity/electron pairs but does not by itself encode the three-dimensional domain geometry.
conditions: Four regions around a centre are arranged tetrahedrally in the introductory VSEPR model.

derivation.action: Preserve the domain count from the Lewis structure.
Place four domains along tetrahedral directions.
derivation.why_valid: Four regions minimise repulsion in a tetrahedral arrangement.

derivation.action: Name electron-domain and molecular geometry separately when lone pairs are present.
derivation.why_valid: The molecular name counts atom positions, not lone-pair directions.

limits: A 2D cross drawing is not evidence of 90° molecular geometry.
checks: NH3: tetrahedral electron-domain geometry but trigonal-pyramidal molecular geometry.

relations.expression: model choice follows requested explanatory output
relations.meaning: VSEPR is the economical model for overall electron-domain arrangement; orbital-overlap/valence-bond descriptions answer orbital composition and overlap questions.
conditions: Choose the model after identifying what the question asks to predict.

derivation.why_valid: Model adequacy is relative to an explanatory task.

derivation.action: Choose VSEPR for overall domain arrangement and orbital overlap for orbital-level bonding detail.
derivation.why_valid: Each model carries a different explanatory scope.

derivation.action: State what the chosen model does not resolve.
derivation.why_valid: A scope boundary prevents treating one model as universally more correct.

limits: Neither model should be presented as universally superior; the question determines the useful level.
checks: For Q5, VSEPR answers the requested overall 3D arrangement without needing orbital wavefunction detail.

relations.expression: sigma: end-on overlap along internuclear axis; pi: side-on overlap with density on opposite sides of the axis
relations.meaning: Sigma/pi classification is defined by overlap symmetry/orientation relative to the internuclear axis, not merely by seeing a single or double bond label.

symbols.meaning: side-on overlap with a nodal plane containing the internuclear axis

conditions: Use the internuclear axis as the reference direction.

derivation.why_valid: The classification is defined relative to this axis.

derivation.action: Classify end-on overlap as sigma and side-on overlap as pi.
derivation.why_valid: The overlap symmetry differs with orientation.

derivation.action: Check for the pi nodal plane through the axis.
derivation.why_valid: This distinguishes side-on pi overlap from axial sigma overlap.

limits: Bond multiplicity is related but is not the defining geometric test.
checks: A pi diagram must place overlap density on opposite sides of the internuclear axis.

teaching_routes.title: Construct hybridisation from electron-domain decisions
entry_needs: Learner can identify atoms, bond order, shared pairs and lone pairs in a supplied simple Lewis structure.
learner_actions: Count domains locally around the selected central atom.
Translate domain count into 3D VSEPR geometry and the introductory hybrid-set mapping.
Choose VSEPR versus orbital-overlap descriptions by explanatory scope.
Classify sigma versus pi overlap from the internuclear axis.
help_plan: Mark the central atom before counting.
Collapse any multiple bond to one VSEPR direction.
Separate electron-domain geometry from molecular geometry.
Ask what the question wants the model to predict before naming a model.
teaching_routes.reveal_plan: Build the local counting and representation rules first, then use Q5 as the model-scope crux and Q6 as the overlap-geometry boundary.

source_preferences.reason: Supports domain counting, geometry and introductory sp2/sp3 mapping.
Supports the internuclear-axis classification used in Q6 and the multiple-bond distinction used in Q2/Q9.

when_not_suitable: Do not extend this slice into delocalisation, resonance-sensitive hybridisation exceptions, radicals, hypervalency or a complete quantum-mechanical treatment.
